meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вспомнили, что у вас есть дочь?
examples.trans: Did you remember that you have a daughter?

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.
Victor Petrovich, what happened?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.en: to film, to take a photo/video of
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take down, remove', paired with 'снимать'.

examples.trans: Wait, do I need to take these off?

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон.
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone.
He took off his coat by the door.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to talk to Katya.

examples.text: Питаюсь плохо, надо к врачу сходить.
examples.trans: I am eating poorly, I should go see a doctor.
I hope this snake does not bite!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, I already know that.
I always remembered her.
Actually, he died recently.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.

examples.text: А я недавно большой кредит взял.
examples.trans: And I recently took out a big loan.
Alright, bye, have a safe trip!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'faster', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Денис, быстро иди работать на кухню!
examples.trans: Denis, quickly go work in the kitchen!
Now quickly look for it everywhere!
Yes, come on faster, let's start!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'begin', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: Yes, come on faster, let's start!
When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У неё на новом месте всё в порядке.
examples.trans: Everything is fine with her at the new place.
Chef, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Сейчас попрощаемся, выпьем, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You are under my roof now.
Now I will have to return my wife's fur coat.
Now you, go ahead and blow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, I already know that.

examples.text: Тебя вспомнишь — и уже не так плохо.
examples.trans: One remembers you, and things do not seem so bad.
Well, there you go, it has started already.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.trans: But he does not know how to cook.

examples.text: Чтобы вкусно её для вас приготовить.
examples.trans: In order to cook it deliciously for you.

examples.text: Только вы же сами её приготовили!
examples.trans: But you cooked it yourself!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And did you ever think of me?
There were difficult moments in life.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They just fired me.

examples.text: По контракту только я могу увольнять.
examples.trans: Under the contract, only I can fire cooks.

examples.text: Дима, я тебя только очень прошу.
examples.trans: Dima, I only ask you very much.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'with teeth' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Just do not be afraid of my teeth.
My tooth hurts.
His wisdom tooth started hurting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'fear'.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.
I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Vitya, meet her right now.

examples.text: Сейчас попрощаемся, выпьем, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.
And where are you going right now?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Но он больше музыкант, чем повар.
examples.trans: But he is more of a musician than a cook.

examples.text: Завтра шеф должен быть на больничном.
examples.trans: Tomorrow the chef must be on sick leave.

examples.text: А я недавно большой кредит взял.
examples.trans: And I recently took out a big loan.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nobody here will touch you.
No, I am going back to work.

examples.text: Нет, мне ваши деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: No, I do not need your money.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: No, it is fine, everything is good.

examples.text: Мы хотим с тобой общаться нормально.
examples.trans: We want to talk with you normally.
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Очень хорошо, и к Кате поближе.
examples.trans: Very good, and closer to Katya.
Denis is a very good guy.
Chef, everything will be fine.

meanings.en: actually, strictly speaking, as a matter of fact
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.
Actually, a rat snake is a non-venomous snake.

examples.text: А вообще-то я ещё не решил.
examples.trans: Actually, I haven't decided yet.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rat snake' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя кухня могла бы спасти положение.
examples.trans: Your cuisine could save the situation.
And also our Far Eastern rat snake.
It pushed the lid open and crawled away!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('poisonous / venomous').

examples.trans: Actually, a rat snake is a non-venomous snake.
Our rat snake is not venomous at all.
Well, of course it is not venomous.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'snake' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нагиев совсем не изменился за это время!
examples.trans: Nagiyev has not changed at all during this time!
Many people consider snakes very cute.

examples.text: Но на змею придётся сегодня скинуться.
examples.trans: But we will have to chip in for the snake today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.
Our head cook there got sick.

examples.text: Нам нужно решить нашу деликатную проблему.
examples.trans: We need to solve our delicate problem.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.

examples.text: Я русский язык вообще не знаю.
examples.trans: I do not know the Russian language at all.

examples.text: Как ты вообще мог это сделать?
examples.trans: How could you do that at all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Excuse me, I need to go.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!
examples.trans: I need to step outside for fresh air urgently!
Mom, please stop him!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, я сейчас помогу отнести вещи.
examples.trans: Of course, I will help carry the things right now.
Well, of course it is not venomous.
Of course I'll help.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.

examples.text: Она ничего об этом не знала.
examples.trans: She knew nothing about it.
He left me this hotel.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я проведу этот вечер просто блестяще!
examples.trans: I will host this evening simply brilliantly!

examples.text: У нас есть девушки лёгкого поведения?
examples.trans: Do we have girls of easy virtue?

examples.text: Помогите, я ведь сам не могу!
examples.trans: Help me, I cannot do it myself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: Ты что, совсем с ума сошёл?
examples.trans: Have you completely lost your mind?

examples.text: Нагиев совсем не изменился за это время!
examples.trans: Nagiyev has not changed at all during this time!
After all, a rat snake is not venomous at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So we will see each other often.
So this is your personal plan?
Then fifty thousand for a rat snake.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'fifty', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Then fifty thousand for a rat snake.
Fifty thousand is great money too!
Fifty metres.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thousand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I am giving you twenty thousand.
Just twenty thousand.

examples.text: Я сто тысяч за это даю!
examples.trans: I am giving a hundred thousand for this!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Alright, good, I understood.

examples.text: Ладно, только ради тебя и природы.
examples.trans: Fine, only for your sake and nature's.
Alright, I will go work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'quite, fully', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Fine, that is quite fair.
That is quite enough.
That is quite enough for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'праведливо'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Fine, that is quite fair.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно справедливо и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite fairly and calmly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And I kiss you too.
Fifty thousand is great money too!
Me too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.trans: It always helps wonderfully.
Fifty thousand is great money too!
It'll be an excellent flat.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы не сможете купить меня за деньги!
examples.trans: You cannot buy me with money!
Did you change your mind and come for the money?

examples.text: Нет, мне ваши деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: No, I do not need your money.
